title: Trace invoke handlers: per-trace fallback lookup when batch_get_trace_infos is unsupported, and fail closed if neither lookup exists
answers: Why does the invoke endpoint fail with an error when my custom tracking store does not support batch trace lookup?
How does the trace ownership check behave for stores that only implement get_trace_info?
Why is a missing trace accepted by the scorer or issue detection invoke endpoint but a foreign one rejected?
body:
Path: The trace-ownership lookup used by the issues/invoke, genai/evaluate/invoke and scorer/invoke endpoints, in mlflow/server/handlers.py:_validate_trace_ids_in_experiment, which calls tracking_store.batch_get_trace_infos.
Rule: Catch both MlflowNotImplementedException and bare NotImplementedError from batch_get_trace_infos, then fall back to get_trace_info per id. Drop only RESOURCE_DOES_NOT_EXIST (a missing trace is simply absent); re-raise all other MlflowException. If get_trace_info also raises NotImplementedError, let it propagate so the request fails closed rather than skipping the check.
Symptom: Before the fix, a plugin store raising a bare NotImplementedError bypassed the fallback, and invoke requests could fail or skip the check depending on the store.
Constraints: Input validation for the same endpoints is separate: trace_ids must be a non-empty list of strings (400 on empty or non-string items), and ids are de-duplicated with dict.fromkeys before lookup; keep these three endpoints aligned.
applies: Trace-ownership checks in invoke handlers that run against a pluggable tracking store.
says: Running evaluation or issue detection on traces fails with an unsupported storage error
Triggering trace scoring fails unexpectedly when connected to our custom storage backend
Trace evaluation jobs should check individual traces if batch retrieval is not supported
Issue detection crashes on custom backends that do not implement bulk trace lookups
Running scorer requests should fail securely when trace ownership cannot be verified

RESOURCE_DOES_NOT_EXIST is dropped while other MlflowException errors are re-raised, and if get_trace_info raises NotImplementedError it propagates to fail closed. This applies to trace-ownership checks in invoke handlers against pluggable tracking stores, with separate input validation requiring non-empty string trace_ids de-duplicated with dict.fromkeys.
